drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna start the mourning ritual with the Nasi?

segments.he: בִּגְדוּלָּה מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל אַהֲרֹן וּלְאֶלְעָזָר וּלְאִיתָמָר״. וּבִקְלָלָה מַתְחִילִין מִן הַקָּטָן — שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה נִתְקַלֵּל נָחָשׁ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְקַלְּלָה חַוָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְקַלֵּל אָדָם!
segments.en: The Gemara cites a baraita which provides the sources for this principle. With regard to matters «of greatness one begins with the greatest» member, «as it is stated: “And Moses said to Aaron, and to Elazar and to Itamar,» his sons” (Leviticus 10:6). Moses first addresses the most important person, Aaron, and this was a matter of distinction, as the verse continues: “For the anointing oil of the Lord is upon you” (Leviticus 10:7). «And» for any matter «involving a curse, one begins with the least» important member of a group, «as the serpent was cursed first, and afterward Eve was cursed and afterward Adam was cursed.»

segments.he: הָא חֲשִׁיבוּתָא לְדִידְהוּ, דְּאָמְרִי לְהוּ: אַתּוּן חֲשִׁיבִיתוּ לְמִיבְעֵי עֲלַן רַחֲמֵי אַכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא.
segments.en: Why, then, are the leaders of the community, its most important members, the first to perform these fast day expressions of mourning, which are a response to a curse? The Gemara answers: The reason is that «this» leadership role in the performance of these acts is considered «a distinction» and an honor «for them, as» it is as though the community is «saying to them: You are worthy of requesting compassion» on behalf «of everyone.»
